summary: Backend-only regression for (1) Safari 'Load failed' CORS fix and (2) new GPS distance-based match filter. 14/14 tests pass against preview URL. Confirmed via raw curl that /api/auth/email-login now returns ACAO:* WITHOUT any access-control-allow-credentials header — the illegal CORS combo that broke Safari fetch() is gone. Distance filter endpoints (save/clear/discover with $geoNear) all behave correctly including edge cases: invalid coords → 400, no-location fallback, max_distance_km=0 fallback, combined with gender filter, and radius-subset consistency (50km ⊂ 300km). Existing flows (discover w/o distance, accepted, likes-received/count, auth/me) still pass.
critical_code_review_comments: CORS fix (allow_credentials=False) is correct and safe given the frontend uses Bearer tokens with credentials:'omit'. Response now has no ACAC header, which is spec-compliant with ACAO:*.
$geoNear pipeline in matches.py correctly rounds distance_km to 1 decimal and returns nearest-first ordering.
GeoJSON order [lng, lat] is correctly enforced in POST /profile/location — good.
Fallback path when caller lacks location is graceful (no 500) — verified.

Suggestion (non-blocking): document/validate max_distance_km lower bound (>0) explicitly in the Pydantic query model to make intent clearer; currently 0 silently falls back which is fine but implicit.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing seeded users (Emma Wilson, Yusuff Adeagbo, Chinyere Jennifer, James Chen, Dr Gerald Marfo).
context_for_next_testing_agent: New test file /app/backend/tests/test_safari_cors_and_distance_edges.py has 9 cases covering Safari CORS regression + distance edge cases. Combined with existing test_location_filter.py (5 cases) = 14 cases, all passing. If retesting CORS, use raw curl and grep for 'access-control-allow-credentials' — it must be absent.
